title: Turnstile priming sandbox notes
body:
Objective:
Quick scratchpad to capture an exploratory benchmark pattern I called 'turnstile priming' — intentionally symmetric, gated arrivals that alternately open and close a burst window to exercise cache/priming behavior and interleaving costs. Want to see how a short rhythm of steady requests -> gated spike -> steady affects p95/p99 when KV cache is partially warm and when quantized kernels are used.

Hypothesis:
- A short gated spike (turnstile) after a long steady stream will amplify tail latency if KV cache eviction/rehydration spans the gating window.
- Small change in batching timeout + allow-listing of warm-cache keys should reduce p99 without hurting throughput.

Test harness (quick):
- Model: open-llm/7B-compatible (benchmark variant: rwi-7b-v1-fp16)
- Hardware: single A10G slot (simulated local runner), 20GB GPU
- Runtime: local-serving binary from gh/pr614 (with latest prefetch KV change)
- Workload generator: custom Go harness (docs in linked PR), arrival pattern config below

Arrival patterns tried:
1) baseline: steady poisson, 50 qps, mean interarrival 20ms, duration 10m
2) turnstile-1: steady 30 qps (5m) -> gate open 400 qps for 8s -> steady 30 qps (5m) -> repeat 6x
3) turnstile-2: same but gate 200 qps for 20s (to test eviction crossing)
4) control: short random microbursts (stochastic) for comparison

Key runtime configs toggled:
- batching_timeout_ms: 6 / 12 / 24
- allowlist_cache_keys: off / on (simple hashed-prefix allowlist to keep a tiny set of keys pinned)
- kv_cache_capacity: 128MB / 512MB
- quant_mode: fp16 / int8-static (quantized kernel fallback enabled)

Quick run log (selected runs):
2024-02-16 09:12: baseline run (poisson, 50qps)
  - p50 24ms, p95 65ms, p99 126ms, sustained throughput 49 qps
2024-02-16 10:04: turnstile-1, batching_timeout_ms=6, allowlist=off, kv=128MB, fp16
  - observed sharp p99 jumps during gate open windows (8s)
  - pre-gate p95 ~70ms, during gate p95 ~220ms, p99 spikes to 980ms (multiple 900-1.1s samples)
  - throughput matched offered load while gate open (393 qps peak)
2024-02-16 11:30: turnstile-1, batching_timeout_ms=12, allowlist=on, kv=512MB, fp16
  - p95 during gate reduced to ~140ms, p99 ~280ms (no 1s spikes)
  - throughput identical, tail reduction significant when allowlist pinned keys
2024-02-17 14:05: turnstile-2, batching_timeout_ms=12, allowlist=on, kv=128MB, int8-static
  - colder KV capacity; saw p99s around 600-900ms intermittently during later gates (eviction likely)
  - int8 path added jitter: p50 slightly lower (~18ms) but p95 widen by ~20ms vs fp16

Observations / notes:
- The most painful spikes happen when the gate opens and many requests reference contexts that were evicted during the idle window. Eviction+rehydration creates a short-term storm of misses and KV fetch overhead plus cache refills that serializes accesses.
- Simple allowlist/pinning of hot keys dramatically reduces observed p99 at modest memory cost. For these workloads there were ~12 keys that accounted for ~40% of requests during the gate windows. Pinning them in KV prevented the cascading miss wave.
- Increasing batching timeout smooths the burst slightly (more coalescing) but at cost of p50; there's an inflection where batching_timeout_ms > ~20ms hurts latency too much for steady load. Aim is 10-12ms for mixed workloads.
- Int8 quant path reduces mean latency but can increase variance; kernel dispatch jitter observed on our A10G build. Need more sampling to confirm.

Mini results table (selected):
Config | gate | p50 | p95 | p99 | notes
--------|------|-----|-----|-----|------
baseline fp16, bt=6, kv128 | none | 24ms | 65ms | 126ms | steady
turn1 fp16, bt=6, kv128 | 400qps x8s | 28ms | 220ms | 980ms | big p99 spikes
turn1 fp16, bt=12, kv512, allowlist | 400qps x8s | 30ms | 140ms | 280ms | tail much better
turn2 int8, bt=12, kv128, allowlist | 200qps x20s | 18ms | 160ms | 720ms | mean good, tail intermittent

Short hypotheses to validate next runs:
- Increase kv_cache_capacity to 1GB and re-run turnstile-2 with int8 => expect tail to shrink (if eviction is root cause)
- Instrument KV eviction timestamps and correlate with p99 spikes (add trace id propagation)
- Test hybrid strategy: pin top-20 hot keys + adaptive batching (increase timeout only when gate open predicted)

Action items / quick TODO:
- [ ] add eviction timestamp tracing to runtime (small patch in gh/pr614)
- [ ] schedule a longer-run (2h) with turnstile-2 + kv=1GB to measure steady-state tail behavior
- [ ] collect kernel-level jitter traces for int8 path on A10G (ask infra for capture)
- [ ] share short slide with product (1-pager) if pinning proves consistent (impact: modest memory + big tail improvement)

Loose thoughts / heuristics from runs:
- For customer-facing SLOs where tail matters, prefer pinning or proactive priming of cache rather than only increasing batch timeouts.
- Turnstile pattern is a realistic proxy for scheduled spike workloads (cron-driven or UI-flurry events) and deserves an automated mitigation path in rollout policies.

Notes to self: keep these runs reproducible—commit harness config into gh/pr614 under experiments/turnstile. Add a small README that describes the gate pattern generator and the key-capture script.

End of scratchpad.
summary: Scratchpad for 'turnstile' gated burst experiments. Observed eviction-driven p99 spikes; allowlisting/pinning of hot keys reduced tails substantially. Next steps: add eviction tracing, try larger KV capacity, and collect int8 kernel jitter traces.
